A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WebThinker research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original WebThinker benchmark and report-generation results, component ablations, backbone-size experiments and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Tables 1–3, Figures 4–5 and Appendix D. Retained results still qualify as original empirical work.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices A/C retain the Deep Web Explorer, document memory, drafting/checking/editing tools, preference-selection rules and iterative online DPO procedure. Shortened explanations do not establish an algorithm or model change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GPQA, GAIA, WebWalkerQA, HLE and Glaive, and retain the same six training datasets. Appendix B confirms unchanged task and domain coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same direct-reasoning models, RAG variants, Search-o1 and proprietary systems. Newly cited tool-learning methods in Related Work are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix B retains 198 GPQA, 103 GAIA, 680 WebWalkerQA, 500 HLE and 30 Glaive evaluation questions. Metrics, judges, evaluation prompts, generation settings and two DPO iterations are unchanged; removing some details from the main text does not establish changed experiments.

E4.justification: Table 3 retains the same training, exploration and report-tool ablations. Figure 5's backbone analysis, Figure 4's t-SNE analysis and Appendix D's case studies are also retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new checklist explains that error bars were omitted because of computational cost, but adds no uncertainty estimates or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: All tabulated and plotted scores and case-study outputs are unchanged. v2 adds introductory comparisons of 21.9% on GAIA and 36.2% on HLE against Search-o1. The HLE percentage follows Figure 1's 11.6 baseline, whereas Table 2 retains 10.8 versus WebThinker's 15.8, implying 46.3%. This is a limited addition to numerical reporting, not new experimental performance.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, their mathematical definitions, generation factorizations and DPO objective are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical results or proofs; shortened surrounding explanations do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The central contributions and claims of improved problem solving and report generation remain the same. The original five-point contribution list is relocated to Appendix E; the introduction's added percentages quantify the retained superiority claim.

C2.justification: New Appendix F discusses misinformation, source bias, privacy and verification risks associated with autonomous web research. The checklist newly attributes absent error bars to computational cost. Existing result interpretations and previously documented modality limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 loses the specification of four nodes with eight H100-80GB GPUs each and the explicit DeepSeek-R1-Distilled-Qwen backbone identification. Appendix C.4 updates the repository reference, and the checklist newly states that model checkpoints are provided. Most hyperparameters and detailed prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related Work adds citations including ReTool, TORL, ToolRL, OTC, RAGEN and RAG-STAR, while dropping works including RetroLLM, SimpleDeepSearcher and AssistRAG. The central positioning against RAG and search-enhanced reasoning remains unchanged. Venue updates and duplicate-reference removal are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: v2 extensively condenses and rewrites the dataset, baseline, implementation, results, ablation and conclusion prose. It moves the contribution list into Appendix E and adds acknowledgments, broader-impact discussion and a conference checklist. These constitute substantial editorial restructuring despite stable scientific content.

P2.justification: The same five figures and ten tables remain, with unchanged scientific display structures. Their placement reflows around the shortened text, while Figure 3 receives small label corrections and Figure 2 a caption correction. There is no substantial graphical redesign.

improvement.justification: The tighter prose, updated references and impact discussion offer limited benefits, but v2 removes useful hardware and backbone-identification details. Its new checklist nevertheless claims compute resources are documented and states that no LLMs were used for research, contradicting the described method and evaluation. The added HLE percentage also carries an existing figure/table discrepancy into the introduction. These modest losses in reproducibility and internal consistency outweigh the editorial gains.
